briefing:
# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Canva, 17 November 2026

**Window covered:** roughly 18 Oct to 17 Nov 2026. Sources below are dated 2 to 15 Nov 2026 unless noted.

## What changed

**Restructuring and layoffs**
- Canva is cutting 22% of its staff, about 1,271 employees, as it flattens its org chart and consolidates teams (https://www.computerworld.com/article/3816579/tech-layoffs-this-year-a-timeline.html). Yahoo Tech puts it at "just over 1,200" (https://tech.yahoo.com/general/breaking-news/article/tech-layoffs-tracker-2026-all-the-job-losses-across-canva-squarespace-amazon-microsoft-apple-meta-and-others-141507340.html).
- CEO Melanie Perkins said Canva must "re-found" itself around "small, empowered teams," and that "small changes won't be enough" (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304).
- Product, growth and platform teams are being merged (https://tech.yahoo.com/general/breaking-news/article/tech-layoffs-tracker-2026-all-the-job-losses-across-canva-squarespace-amazon-microsoft-apple-meta-and-others-141507340.html).
- Departing staff get at least six months' salary plus support (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304), keep their company MacBooks and receive a free year of LinkedIn Premium (https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/world-news/canva-layoffs-2026-meet-ceo-melanie-perkins-who-plans-to-give-away-80-of-her-billion-dollar-fortune-as-1271-jobs-are-cut/articleshow/135575689.cms).
- Capital Brief reported that Canva could announce further redundancies or a hiring freeze in November. Canva has not confirmed this (https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137).
- Capital Brief also reported finance-division cuts of 32 roles in January, which were previously unreported (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).

**AI and partnerships**
- Canva expanded its OpenAI deal, gaining broader access to GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6. The companies will work on lowering running costs, though no figures were disclosed. This came days after Canva launched its second in-house AI model (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- OpenAI already powers Canva Code, which builds interactive designs, websites and apps from text prompts (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).

**Marketing**
- Canva launched a new North America brand platform, "What Will You Canva Today?", created by agency GS&P, with TV spots, out-of-home and social work (https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/419113/canva-unveils-campaign-by-new-agency-gsp.html).

**Deals and hires**
- A wire report says a company agreed to be acquired by Globex Corporation for $9.4 billion, expected to close next quarter. The snippet does not name Canva. **Treat as unconfirmed for Canva** (https://wire-briefs.example/deals/acquisition-announced).
- No Canva hires or senior appointments in the window were found in the results.

## Caveats
- Layoff figures vary slightly (1,271 vs. "just over 1,200").
- The Capital Brief hiring-freeze and finance-cut reports are secondhand.
- A Canva profile lists earlier acquisitions (e.g., Ortto, Doohly), but these fall outside the 30-day window and are undated in the source, so they are excluded (https://tavily.com/knowledge/company/wafeqPWRLzYp).

## Open questions
1. With the restructure merging product, growth and platform teams, who are our current counterparts, and which workstreams are being deprioritized or delayed into 2027?
2. Has Canva confirmed whether any further redundancies or a hiring freeze are coming in November, and how would that affect our support and delivery timelines?
3. Does the expanded OpenAI partnership change pricing, data handling or feature availability for enterprise customers, and is the Globex transaction relevant to us in any way?
